standard.title: Composite shapes from familiar shapes
standard.description: Represent and approximate composite shapes and objects in the environment, using combinations of familiar shapes and objects
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can make, compare and classify objects by key features (AC9M3SP01). They have not yet formally decomposed complex shapes into familiar components or used this decomposition to represent real-world objects.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students represent and approximate composite shapes and objects using combinations of familiar 2D shapes and 3D objects.

nodes.label: Identify components of composite shapes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the familiar shapes that make up a composite shape or object.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the familiar shapes within one composite shape; list the components.
nodes.typical_width: Identify familiar 2D shapes within composite designs (logos, natural objects, architectural features); identify the 3D objects that make up a complex object; re-create identified components using physical or virtual materials.
wider: Analyse logos or graphic designs to identify all geometric components, discussing how designers use primitive shapes to create recognisable images
Deconstruct cartoon characters or illustrations into their geometric components, listing all shapes present
success_criteria: Students can identify and name the familiar shapes that make up a given composite shape
Students can re-create the composite using those component shapes

nodes.label: Construct and approximate composite shapes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can combine familiar shapes to construct or approximate composite shapes and real-world objects.
nodes.minimum_width: Construct one composite shape using at least two familiar shapes; explain which shapes were combined.
nodes.typical_width: Use physical or virtual materials to construct composite shapes approximating real objects; use cube grids to model 3D objects; draw cartoon animals or objects using geometric primitives; create simple logos using combinations of shapes.
wider: Design a logo using graphic design software, combining geometric shapes purposefully and explaining how each shape contributes to the overall design
Build virtual 3D environments using cube-based software, making decisions about how to approximate curved surfaces and organic shapes with cubes and explaining the limitations of the approximation
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Constructing composite shapes — especially in design and digital contexts — develops spatial reasoning and connects geometry to authentic creative and technical applications. Students who engage with design software or 3D construction tools develop a richer geometric vocabulary.
success_criteria: Students can combine at least two familiar shapes to construct or represent a composite shape
Students can explain which familiar shapes were combined and how they fit together
